items.title: Junior Mance Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995…
items.q: I worked with Dinah Washington for two weeks... I had no problems with Dinah. She gave me complete freedom as to how to play behind her.

ctx.x: But there are people too, like I worked with Dinah Washington for two weeks. She played in the church you know, and sang in it too. She also played piano. Because the good thing about working with her, you know she would sometimes show me what chords she would prefer to others, but they were never like just a simple one-three-five type chords. She knew the others too. Sarah Vaughan was another one who played and sang in church, and she was a piano player once, a lot of people don’t know this, in Earl Hines’ band,…
Well I was listening to an interview of yours on one of your records in “Jazzspeak,” and you were talking about how you learned from your father and —

items.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: He has recorded and toured with Dizzy Gillespie, Dinah Washington and Joe Williams

ctx.x: Is that — that’s not from that jam session album with Dinah Washington?
No, this is with Cannonball and Nat. The tune is called “Spectacular.”
